result:
**No. Logout doesn't remove the FCM token on the server.** A case-insensitive search of non-spec files under `src` for `logout` and `sign-out` found nothing. There is no server logout handler, so nothing there calls the FCM service.

Three things deactivate tokens today. All of them soft-delete by setting `isActive: false` and `deletedAt`:

1. **Explicit client call:** `DELETE /fcm/unregister-token/:deviceId` (`src/fcm/fcm.controller.ts:51-65`) calls `unregisterDeviceToken` (`src/fcm/fcm.service.ts:127-132`). The app has to call this itself before or during logout. Nothing on the server forces it.
2. **Registering a new token:** `registerDeviceToken` (`src/fcm/fcm.service.ts:97-103`) calls `unregisterAllDeviceTokens` (`src/fcm/fcm.service.ts:146-150`). This deactivates every token the user has, on all devices, so a login on a new device removes the old device's token.
3. **Pruning after a failed send:** `removeInvalidTokens` (`src/fcm/fcm.service.ts:283`) is private and never called, per my earlier notes. I only matched it by grep this time and didn't re-read it. It doesn't prune anything today.

If the app doesn't call the unregister endpoint on logout, the logged-out device keeps its active token. It will keep getting that user's pushes until another registration replaces the token.
